name: zeroshot
note: The regime curve: how much unlabelled target data does the model actually need? Every published cross-subject number in this literature sits at ONE point on this axis, almost always the loosest (`transductive`), and almost never says so. This sweep holds the architecture fixed and varies only the regime, so the x-axis is the deliverable. `regime` is declared overridable because varying it IS the experiment -- and every arm still pays the identical recipe otherwise.

arms.name: inductive
arms.prediction: the floor, and the only literally zero-shot number here. Nothing from the target subject at all. Expect a large drop -- this is the quantity every 'calibration-free' claim is implicitly compared against and nobody reports.

arms.name: inductive_srcalign
arms.prediction: one reference estimated from the training pool and applied to the target. Isolates how much of alignment's benefit needs TARGET data versus merely needs a common reference frame.

arms.name: calib1
arms.prediction: one unlabelled trial; probably unstable even with shrinkage

arms.name: calib5
arms.prediction: the interesting point: if 5 unlabelled trials recover most of the transductive number, calibration-free operation is real and the deployment story is a 20-second recording.

arms.name: calib50
arms.prediction: expected to be within noise of transductive

arms.name: transductive
arms.prediction: the ceiling for this family, and what the literature usually reports as 'cross-subject'

arms.name: transductive_ttbn
arms.prediction: recomputing BatchNorm statistics on the target on TOP of alignment. Published gains for this measured it as an ALTERNATIVE to alignment, not stacked on it, so temper the prior sharply -- and check n_bn_adapted is nonzero before reading a null result.
